svg.title: Urna Aberta: how a ballot goes from an offline machine to a blockchain and a verifier
svg.desc: Animated explainer in 7 scenes of 8 seconds, following one symbolic receipt R7. 1: Not just voting, being able to check later: the offline machine encrypts, the blockchain records, a public verifier checks; the receipt goes back with the voter. 2: The machine encrypts the choice and prints signed receipt R7 before the decision; the receipt names no candidate and R7 is only a symbolic locator code. 3: CONFIRM keeps R7 encrypted for the tally; the alternative TEST opens and checks the choice, voids that ballot and the voter votes again. 4: When polls close, the machine signs one batch containing R7 and sends it as a transaction to the Solidity contract on the blockchain, which accepts a registered machine, one batch, before the deadline, and rejects an invalid signature or a second batch. 5: Three of five trustees publish decryption shares with proofs, only for the audited total, to the blockchain. 6: An independent verifier reads the public export, checks the full signed receipt R7, its inclusion in the batch, the proofs, and recounts; if R7 goes missing, the check flags it. 7: The machine encrypts, the blockchain records, you check. Educational prototype; local blockchain in the demo.

g.text: Not just voting. Being able to check later.
A proposal: offline machine + public BLOCKCHAIN + independent verifier.
The polling bulletin reports station totals. Here, a receipt lets you check ballot inclusion.
receipt R7 stays with you and goes to the verifier
It encrypts your vote and prints receipt R7.
The receipt comes before your decision and names no candidate.
Illustrative example · R7 is a symbolic code: it locates the ballot, it does not identify you.
CONFIRM keeps R7 encrypted for the tally.
TEST is the alternative: open the choice, void that ballot, vote again.
Testing helps catch a lying machine, but cannot guarantee catching every fraud.
The machine signs one batch and sends it.
A Solidity contract accepts registered machines, one batch, before the deadline.
Ballots go up as one batch after closing, not one by one. Your receipt stays with you.
3 of 5 key holders help decrypt the sum.
Each trustee holds part of the key, publishing a contribution and proof on the blockchain.
A protocol and API rule, not immunity: 3 colluding trustees could open ballots.
Only the total is opened. Each ballot, R7 included, stays encrypted.
The public trustee API only produces shares of the audited total.
An independent verifier checks your R7.
It reads the public blockchain export, finds R7 in the signed batch, recounts.
R7 only locates. The full signed receipt, checked with the proofs, is the evidence.
R7 is in machine 1's signed batch
The machine encrypts. The blockchain records. You check.
The bulletin reports totals. Here, also check that your ballot was included.
Educational prototype · local blockchain in the demo (one Anvil node) · not production-ready.
